node.statement: Complete the supremum argument by splitting on the domain E_n:=M_n tensor S_P. If E_n={0}, then the bounded linear map h_n:E_n->B((S_{P,Q})^n) is the zero map, hence b_n=||h_n||=0, and b_n^2 <= (1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e holds because C_prod*e>=0. If E_n is nonzero, its unit sphere is nonempty (normalize any nonzero vector), and the definition of the operator norm of the bounded linear map h_n gives b_n=sup_{||Z||=1}||h_n(Z)||. Since all values are nonnegative and b_n is finite by 1.2.3.1, sup_{||Z||=1}||h_n(Z)||^2=(sup_{||Z||=1}||h_n(Z)||)^2=b_n^2. Taking the supremum in the pointwise inequality of 1.2.3.2 therefore yields b_n^2 <= (1+kappa*e)b_n+C_prod*e. Thus the scalar inequality holds in both cases, including the allowed zero corner.
